facts.text: Mud Bay has long been part of the traditional territory of the Tlingit people, specifically the Jilkaat (Chilkat) and Lkoot (Chilkoot) groups.
Mud Bay sits on the Chilkat Peninsula, flanked by Chilkoot Inlet to the east and Chilkat Inlet to the west, extending south to Seduction Point.
Mud Bay's tidal fluctuations expose mudflats and marshes that support intertidal communities and nutrient‑rich sediments, while surrounding forests host Sitka spruce, western hemlock, and red alder.
Mud Bay is a prime stopover for shorebirds and waterfowl during spring and fall migrations, with best viewing one to two hours before high tide.
Mud Bay enjoys a maritime climate with mild temperatures, high humidity, and about 60 inches of precipitation annually, mostly rain and some winter snowfall.
The coastal‑marsh habitat of Mud Bay supports brown bears, moose, porcupines, year‑round bald eagles, and migratory waterfowl such as surf scoters.
